name: State
description: While it is intended to be used in conjunction with the UI library, state management has many use-cases outside of this.

functions.name: createSignal
description: Creates a "signal" with a given initial value.
Signals form the backbone of a reactive system, allowing other code to observe their changes and run side effects accordingly.
When read from within a tracking scope (e.g. `createEffect`), will add the signal to the list of observed signals in the scope,
causing the scope's observer to react to updates.

returns.name: get
returns.description: Returns the current value of the signal.

returns.name: set
returns.description: Sets the value of the signal and notifies all observers of the change.

functions.name: createEffect
description: Creates an "effect" which is triggered when any of the signals it uses are updated.
Simply calling the getter of a signal within the callback will cause the effect to observe changes.
All observers and any child effects will be cleaned up when the effect is re-run,
allowing you to conditionally create effects or listen to a second signal based on the value of the first.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.description: Callback to execute when any observed signals are updated.

functions.name: createMemo
description: Memoises a value so that it's only recomputed when one of the observed signals changes.
The value returned is itself a signal, so that downstream effects are updated when the memoised value is recomputed.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.description: Callback to execute when any observed signals are updated. Same as an effect.

returns.name: get
returns.description: Returns the current value of the memo. Same as a signal's getter.

functions.name: untrack
description: Executes the callback immediately and without a tracking scope.
This allows for reading the values of signals inside of effect callbacks without observing future changes.

returns.description: Any values will be returned by `untrack`.

functions.name: onCleanup
description: Registers a cleanup hook within the current tracking scope.
Will be called when the scope is disposed (e.g. when the parent of a nested effect is rerun, or a component is unmounted).
Any signals read within the callback will not be tracked.
